document.title: Politburo Session, January 21, 1987
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan Déjà vu? Lessons from the Soviet Experience
document.note: The Politburo discusses the results of Shevardnadze and Dobrynin's trip to Afghanistan. Shevardnadze's report is blunt and pessimistic about the war and the internal situation. The Politburo's main concern is how to end the war but save face and ensure a friendly, neutral Afghanistan.

persons.name: Eduard Shevardnadze
persons.role: Soviet Foreign Minister; reported on visit to Afghanistan with Dobrynin

persons.role: Soviet official who visited Afghanistan with Shevardnadze

Najib was complaining about the petty patronizing on the part of our advisers.
Najib has agreed to this step (national reconciliation) finally.

I do not believe that the question of Afghanistan is being decided in Islamabad.  It is being decided in Washington.

persons.role: CPSU General Secretary chairing the session

We have to take a firm line to withdraw from there within two years.

events.description: Politburo session discussing Shevardnadze and Dobrynin's visit to Afghanistan and withdrawal strategy.
National reconciliation policy launched in Afghanistan.
Politburo session discussing Shevardnadze and Dobrynin's report on Afghanistan and the withdrawal and national reconciliation policy.
Shevardnadze and Dobrynin visited Afghanistan and met Najib.
National reconciliation policy was announced by the Afghan government, marking big changes in Afghanistan.
The USSR gave Afghanistan 100 million rubles of free assistance, which went to the elite.
Pravda reported that 400 representatives came to Kabul amid national reconciliation.
Politburo confirmed its firm line and tasked the Commission for Afghanistan with drafting decisions, with withdrawal aimed within two years.

relationships.detail: Najib depends on Soviet support.
relationships.quote: The main thing is material and political support for Najib.

relationships.detail: Keshtamand is Prime Minister.
relationships.quote: invite Keshtamand (the Prime Minister)

relationships.detail: Najib took over from Karmal.
relationships.quote: We pressured Karmal to do it for a whole year, and with no result.

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze and Dobrynin made a joint visit to Afghanistan, and Shevardnadze reported on its results to the Politburo.
relationships.quote: About the Results of [Eduard] Shevardnadze and [Anatoly] Dobrynin's Visit to Afghanistan.

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze met Najib during the visit and formed a very good impression of him.
relationships.quote: Najib leaves a very good impression.  However, not everybody supports him, even in the leadership.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev says he told Najib that the Afghans must strengthen their army and that the USSR would support it.
relationships.quote: I told Najib that they have to strengthen the army, that we will support it

relationships.detail: Chebrikov says Gorbachev had already spoken to Karmal about national reconciliation.
relationships.quote: All this, Mikhail Sergeyevich, you have already said to Karmal.  That's how the idea of national reconciliation emerged.

relationships.detail: The Soviets pressured Karmal for a year to adopt national reconciliation, without result.
relationships.quote: We pressured Karmal to do it for a whole year, and with no result.

relationships.detail: Najib agreed to national reconciliation, which Karmal had resisted under Soviet pressure; Najib is implicitly Karmal's successor.
relationships.quote: Najib has agreed to this step (national reconciliation) finally.  We pressured Karmal to do it for a whole year

relationships.detail: Najib is treated as the Afghan leader whom the USSR must support politically and materially.
relationships.quote: The main thing is material and political support for Najib.  There is no other solution.

relationships.detail: Keshtmand is identified as the Afghan Prime Minister, whom Ryzhkov proposes to invite to Moscow.
relationships.quote: I support the proposal to invite Keshtamand (the Prime Minister).

relationships.detail: Ryzhkov supports inviting Keshtmand to Moscow to hear Afghan requests.
relationships.quote: I support the proposal to invite Keshtamand (the Prime Minister).  To listen what requests they have.

relationships.detail: Mojahadeen leaders declined reconciliation with the PDPA government.
relationships.quote: the leaders of the mojahadeen made a miscalculation having declined reconciliation.

relationships.detail: Soviet garrisons are shelled by rebel forces, and the war cannot be won militarily.
relationships.quote: The number of shelling of our garrisons has doubled.  They are mainly shooting from the hamlets

relationships.detail: Sokolov reports the 40th Army's casualties and the military situation to the Politburo.
relationships.quote: The 40th army has already lost 1,280 men in 1986.

relationships.detail: Soviet troops are stationed in Afghanistan and are slated for withdrawal.
relationships.quote: To withdraw three regiments, but, as some people propose, to continue aerial attacks from the Soviet territory?

relationships.detail: Sokolov lists KGB channels among the means to be used for the Afghan line.
relationships.quote: diplomatic, along the KGB lines, public relations, political [means], and material assistance.

relationships.detail: Chebrikov was KGB chairman, though this is not stated in the text.
relationships.quote: Chebrikov. We are discussing the Afghan question more than other [issues].

relationships.detail: Gorbachev proposes launching foreign policy mechanisms through UN mediator Cordovez.
relationships.quote: to launch foreign policy mechanisms through Cordovez, through Pakistan.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev proposes working through Pakistan on the Afghan settlement.
relationships.quote: to launch foreign policy mechanisms through Cordovez, through Pakistan.

relationships.detail: Gromyko proposes a closed conversation with the Americans about the Durand line.
relationships.quote: We have to start a conversation, a closed one, with the Americans, about the Durand line.

relationships.detail: Gromyko agrees with Shevardnadze's characterization of Najib and suggests coalition government with his consent.
relationships.quote: I agree with the characterization of Najib.

relationships.detail: The Politburo under Gorbachev decides on the withdrawal of Soviet troops in two years.
relationships.quote: [Let us] push Najib and to finish it all in two years.

relationships.detail: Ligachev speaks as a Politburo member.
relationships.quote: Ligachev.  We cannot bring them freedom by the military way.

relationships.detail: Pakistan does not let Afghan refugees return through its territory.
relationships.quote: Refugees started returning.  Although Pakistan does not let them through.

key_claims: Shevardnadze argued the Soviet war effort had been a failure and needed a political decision.
Politburo members agreed to pursue national reconciliation and withdrawal within about two years.
A hired Afghan army and continued material aid were considered substitutes for Soviet troops.
Marshal Sokolov said the war cannot be won militarily; 40th Army lost 1,280 men in 1986.
